steps: Curl your thumb down onto your palm while extending your pinky finger upward, folding your middle three fingers down too.
Hold the hand up in front of your shoulder, in the signing space at about chin height.
Keep the handshape perfectly still and steady — the number six has no movement of its own.
Face the back of your hand outward toward the person you are signing to, away from yourself.
Keep a neutral, matter-of-fact expression when signing a number in isolation.
tip: Numbers 6–9 are palm-out while 1–5 are palm-in when signed alone — mixing them up is the classic beginner mistake.

steps: Open your dominant hand into a flat five handshape, spreading all five fingers wide.
Touch the tip of your thumb to the center of your chest, just below your collarbone.
Slide the hand a few inches outward and away from your chest, leading with the thumb.
Keep the palm angled slightly toward yourself as the hand glides forward off the chest.
Smile softly or keep a relaxed face — this sign means being okay, not making a payment.
tip: Never use this for fee, cost, thin, or small — Lifeprint warns the sign only covers feeling okay or something being cool.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand out in front of you, flat and open with the palm facing down.
Rest the fingertips of your dominant hand on the back of that hand, starting in a flat O handshape.
Slide the dominant hand outward across the back of the base hand while opening it into a spread five handshape.
Repeat the short outward slide a second time — the noun form uses two quick movements.
Keep both palms facing down the whole time, as if laying opinions out on a table for someone.
tip: The verb advise uses one long movement; the noun advice repeats it twice, short and quick.

steps: Curl both hands into tight A fists, pressing each thumb firmly against the folded index finger.
Raise your right A fist to your chest and your left A fist to the left side of your abdomen.
Start with both fists hovering about two inches out from your body.
Thump both fists inward against your body twice in a quick in-out-in double motion.
Keep both palms facing toward your body for the entire movement, like gripping a rifle.
Hold a straight, upright posture with a serious, matter-of-fact expression.
tip: Picture both fists gripping a rifle held across the chest — the mime is the memory hook for this sign.

steps: Open both hands into relaxed five handshapes, spreading your fingers wide apart.
Hold both hands about an inch in front of your upper chest, thumbs closest to your body.
Brush both hands straight down your chest as if smoothing a shirt, letting the thumbs drag lightly.
Repeat the downward brush a second time in a quick double movement.
Angle your palms slightly toward yourself so the thumbs stay near your chest as they slide.
Keep a neutral expression — actual chest contact is optional; the double brush is what counts.
tip: One large single brush downward means DRESS or GOWN, not clothes — the double movement is the tell.

steps: Bend your dominant index finger into an X handshape: a loose fist with the index finger hooked.
Hold the X hand out in front of you, slightly to the right of center.
Snap the hand downward from the wrist in one firm stroke, ending with the palm facing down.
Start the stroke with the palm facing forward, then let it rotate to palm-down as you bend.
Use a strong, urgent facial expression — the harder and faster the stroke, the more mandatory it feels.
tip: This is the same production Lifeprint glosses as need, must, and have-to — keep it forceful to carry the 'no choice' sense.
